check: whether the 76 tests added this session actually executed and passed, which I had verified only by count and compilation
why: I had confirmed the tests exist and compile. Neither shows that they ran. A test added after the last JUnit invocation would compile and sit unexecuted, and the pass figure would not notice.
method: Took the nine classes added this session and looked for each one's JUnit XML, reading tests, failures and errors from the file rather than trusting the count.
itAlsoCorroboratesTheReport: The section-1b table claims 66 unit tests across seven of these classes. The XML for those seven sums to 66 exactly - 8, 9, 6, 13, 10, 9 and 11 - and the two remaining classes are GameTest rather than unit tests, which is why they are not in that count.

twoScaresThatResolved.first: I read the XML write time as 11:33:38 and the newest commit as 11:33:50, twelve seconds later, and concluded the mixin test had never run. The file's own timestamp field reads 11:31:45 - the write happens when the run finishes - so the test ran before the commit that described it.
twoScaresThatResolved.second: Searching for each class by bare name found no XML, which looked like nine unexecuted classes. The files exist under their package-qualified names, such as ...greatwall.gameplay.BeaconLedgerTest.xml.
twoScaresThatResolved.lesson: Both came from inferring a fact from an adjacent one - a write time for a run time, and a filename shape for existence - rather than reading the field or listing the directory.
